I added `src/db.py`. `get_conn()` returns `psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"], prepare_threshold=None)`. I haven't run it or the tests.

I set `prepare_threshold=None` because of a stored project note. In production and staging, connections go through a transaction-mode pooler on port 6432, and server-side prepared statements fail there with "prepared statement does not exist". Local Postgres has no pooler, so that failure would only appear after deploy. The setting does no harm locally.

If `DATABASE_URL` isn't set, `get_conn()` raises `KeyError`. I didn't add a fallback, so a misconfigured deploy fails right away instead of connecting to the wrong database.

The caller is responsible for closing the connection, ideally with `with get_conn() as conn:`. The same note says to keep transactions short and not hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger.
